rendered: The document does not say that the EG process corroded the aluminium foil. It reports the opposite. In general terms, aluminium foils are reactive and easily subject to corrosion during separation, which can contaminate the active materials.[1] For the EG-based process, the aluminium foils were fully recovered with shiny surfaces, which the authors read as no corrosion.[2][3] The XRD pattern showed only aluminium peaks, so the authors concluded that the process does not corrode aluminium.[4] The corrosion the document does describe happens in water, not in EG. Water was rejected because the aluminium foil corroded due to lithium leaching from the NMC cathode, which made the water solution basic.[5][6] The authors state that such corrosion would contaminate the NMC particles by forming Al(OH)3 precipitates on the cathode surfaces.[7][8] Because the document reports no corrosion for the EG process, it describes no corrosion product and no step for removing a corrosion product. The recovered foils were clean, with no residues left.[9]
